texts.facts: It is submitted that in fact Bhuruji S/o Rumal Singh (PW-1) is the author of FIR (Ex.P/1). In the FIR, he had not taken name of accused Subhash. Subhash was identified for the first time in the court along with named accused Vahariya and Gyan Singh. This witness has admitted in para 5 of his cross-examination that for the first time he had identified the accused persons before the Court and prior to that no Test Identification Parade was carried out in front of any Magistrate. It is submitted that this witness has admitted that there was a sudden altercation on account of the fact that all the Baratis were under the influence of alcohol (beer/whiskey) and then dispute had occurred. This witness has admitted that there was huge crowd and he cannot state as to which of the persons had an altercation with which of the accused persons. This witness has also admitted that there were several other persons of public in the crowd. He admits that he had seen the witnesses for the first time. It is pointed out that this evidence was taken on 19.12.2011 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:12162 3 CRA-770-2016 whereas admittedly the incident took place on 06.06.2011. Thus, after more than six months, identification of unknown persons is impossible and on the basis of said identification, at least those who have not been named in the FIR, cannot be convicted. 3. It is also submitted that the dead body of Rama was admittedly recovered from Tapti river basin and diatom test in regard to said finding that cause of death was drowning is made out from the report dated 28.01.2016 furnished by Medico Legal Institute, Government of Madhya Pradesh Home (Police) Department, Gandhi Medical College Building, Bhopal vide dispatch No. Q / MLI/BIO/Diatom-371/11. In report it is mentioned that articles 'bone' and 'water' are found positive for diatom test. Thus, it is submitted that in an incident which had no pre-planning or any intention or mens ria took place at the spur of the moment when the persons who were hurt being part of a marriage party were requested to stop drinking and consume their food when they started pelting stones and then stones were pelted from both the sides. Thus, it is submitted that present being a case of death due to drowning and injuries which were found on the body of Rama in postmortem could have been caused on account of drowning, present is a fit case for acquittal. 4. Reading from cross-examination of author of FIR, Bhuruji (PW-1), it is pointed out that this witness admits that the dead body of Rama was recovered from a waterbody. There was huge block of stones on both the sides. They were 30-40 ft height. He admits that some people had run towards the bridge. Rama had come from behind and was running ahead of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:12162 4 CRA-770-2016 them. He had fallen down on two three occasions before climbing the rocks and as soon as he climbed the rocks, he had fallen down in the water. This witness admits that Prem Singh, Sunita and he himself had also sustained injuries on account of fall while running. In para 11, this witness admits that for the first time he is stating before the Court that Gyan Singh and Subhash had hit him with a stone. Thus, it is submitted that in a sudden Mukesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37648470/ 2 altercation if some members of the complainant party started running under the influence of alcohol and had sustained injuries due to fall, then conviction of the appellants cannot be sustained as cause of death is not because of any ante mortem injury but due to drowning. Evidence of Bhuruji (PW-1) is unrebuttable. It is about 8 kms away from Nepanagar. Bhuruji (PW-1) had lodged a report against Gyan Singh S/o Mangilal Bhilala, Kashiram S/o Gathiya Barela, Ratan S/o Gathiya, Jatan S/o Gathiya, Vahariya S/o Gangadas, Balvant S/o unknown, Thakur S/o unknown, Madu S/o unknown that he is a resident of village Jamthi Police Station Shahpur and is an agriculturist. At village Jamthi, there was marriage function of Subhash S/o Nakhla. In Barat of Subhash, several persons, namely, Rangiya S/o Chamariya, Rem Singh S/o Hirman, Bhur Singh S/o NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:12162 5 CRA-770-2016 Manga, Mool Singh S/o Jawan Singh, Patliya S/o Rumal Singh, Manga S/o Jaam Singh, Sardar S/o Kutar Singh, Rama S/o Khoom Singh, ladies and children had come to village Davalikhurd in the Barat. After reaching Davalikhurd, they started dancing. On this dancing episode, there was an altercation with Gyan Singh S/o Mangilal Bhilala. When Gyan Singh had collected other persons and then they started throwing stones and beating the Baratis. As a result of which, Baratis started running. Spot Map is Ex.P/3 showing the place where pelting of stones had taken place. In this spot map, the position of river is not shown. It is not mentioned that what is the distance of the river from where the dead body was recovered. Another spot map is Ex.P/19 showing the position of river and pointing out that point No.5 is the road towards village Davalikhurd where the incident took place and dead body was recovered from the riverbed marked as ' X' and shown as (1) on the spot map (Ex.P/19). 7. Bhuruji (PW-1) after making general and omnibus allegations in para 5 admits that for the first time he had identified three persons before the Court, namely, Vahariya, Gyan Singh and Subhash. He admits that prior to that no such identification proceedings were drawn either before the police or before the Magistrate. This witness admits that dispute had occurred on account of food and drinks. He admits that he had seen the accused persons prior to his deposition outside the Court. He admits that no identification was carried out by the police either at Police Station or Jail. 8. This witness admits that Baghnala is at a distance of 2-3 kms from bus stand fatak and it is further at a distance of 2-3 kms from river Tapti. This NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:12162 6 CRA-770-2016 witness admits in para 8 of his cross-examination that Rama had fallen down from the rocks and prior to that he had fallen down on 2-3 occasions, as a result of which he had sustained injuries. On account of his fall from the rock, he had fallen in the waterbody. This witness has also admitted that Premsingh, Sunita and he himself had sustained injuries due to fall. Mukesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37648470/ 3 9. In para 11 this witness admits that for the first time he was stating before the Court that Gyan Singh and Subhash had hit them with stones. He has admitted that incident had for the first time taken place at the shop of Pyar Singh. The shop of Pyar Singh is not shown in the spot map (Ex.P/3). Therefore, it is admitted by Bhuruji (PW-1) that in fact incident had not taken place at the house of Gyan Singh but at the shop of Pyar Singh. Bhuruji (PW-1) states that he was asked by Nahar Singh (PW-6) to lodge report at 11-11.30 p.m. but he had returned back to Nepa. FIR (Ex.P/1) was recorded on 07.06.2011 at Nepanagar at 10.45 a.m. It does not contain the name of Subhash. This witness admits in para 14 of his cross- examination that Barat had reached village Davli between 12-1.00 noon. They had their lunch at about 3.00 p.m. The dispute with the villagers was settled to reconciliation. He was not present at the time of reconciliation. He admits that the place where the dead body of Rama was recovered has huge rocky structures. 10. Bhoorsingh (PW-2) admits that he was taking name of Gyan Singh, Subhash and Vahariya for the first time. During his interrogation by the police he had not taken their names. In para 4, this witness admits that as per their traditions, children, ladies and gents drink alcohol and make NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:12162 7 CRA-770-2016 themselves merrier. He admits that driver and conductor of the bus were also present but they have not been examined by the prosecution as they could have been independent witnesses. Bhoorsingh (PW-2) admits that distance of Baghnala is about 4 kms from Davalikhurd and then 1 km beyond Baghnala is the river. There are huge rocky structures around the river. In para 6 this witness admits that Rama was running ahead of them and he was followed by Bhurji, Nakhla, Manga, Nahar Singh, Sardar Singh, Moon Singh, Patliya and Subhash. This witness admits that Rama had fallen down in the river. The villagers had consumed the Namkeen and alcohol and had slept. This witness admits that persons residing in Tapras near the place of incident, have no enmity with them. He admits that from Davalikhurd, if one has to travel towards the river, then one has to pass through bus stand and the Tapras situated near the bus stand. Each of the motorcycles was carrying 2-3 persons. He admits that when police was preparing Lash (Dead body) Panchnama, prior to that accused persons were taken to the police station at their instance. This witness admits that the place where dead body of Rama was NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:12162 8 CRA-770-2016 lying is surrounded by huge rocks. Pointed rocky structures are available where dead body was recovered. The river bedrock also contains rocky structures. He admits that he had not sustained any injury. This witness admits that when they had reached the bridge over the river then police personnel had come. They had sent the injured for treatment and had taken remaining persons to the police station. They had taken them to the house of the bride. Mukesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37648470/ 4 11. Sardar Singh (PW-3) identified only Gyan Singh and stated that he does not know the names of any other persons. In cross-examination, this witness states that stone pelting was carried out from a distance of about 200 feet. Sardar Singh (PW-3) also admitted that they had climbed rocks and had sustained injuries out of anxiety. There was no enmity with them. Naharsingh (PW-6) admits that he was informed that dead body of Rama was found inside Tapti river. Police had prepared Panchnama in front of him. He admits that the Sarpanch of village Jamthi all the witnesses are his voters. 15. Moon Singh (PW-7) admits in para 4 that since they were demanding alcohol at the shop of Pyar Singh and he was not supplying alcohol, that was the cause of the dispute. There Mukesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37648470/ 5 were 400-500 people at the spot. 16. Subhash (PW-8) admits that on the next day of the incident, Nahar Singh had informed him that since Rama had fallen down in Tapti river, he died. He admits that Nahar Singh had informed him that Baratis had entered into altercation amongst themselves and stone pelting took place amongst themselves. 17. Dr. Syed Tarique (PW-9) had carried out MLC on Mohan Singh, Sardar Singh, Magga S/o Jam Singh, Patliya S/o Rumal Singh and found that their injuries were simple in nature caused by hard and blunt object. 18. Dr. Ramesh Somani (PW-11) stated that Magga S/o Jam Singh had suffered fracture of scapula bone which could have been caused due to fall of Magga. Others who were subjected to radiological examination had not suffered any fracture. Ravishankar Kokde (PW-12) had prepared spot map (Ex.P/3). Dead body of Rama was taken out from waterbody vide Panchnama (Ex.P/20). He had issued Safina form. He had collected certain pieces of stones vide Ex.P/6. He had also collected water in a bottle from the place where the dead body was recovered vide Ex.P/22. Admittedly, the dead body was subjected to postmortem and thereafter femur bone was preserved for diatom test.
